title: 小小英文新鲜事 - 1010 | 百年新野猫、金字塔鳄鱼、太空皮卡丘
ending_game: Lina 的无厘头二选一：抱抱小野猫，还是骑在鳄鱼化石背上？你选哪个？

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Hey everyone, welcome back! I'm Mia.

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: And I'm Lina! It's Saturday, October tenth!

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: We've got three brand-new stories for you today! All super fresh!

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: Fresh like my socks? I changed them today!

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Ha! Even fresher! Story one! Scientists found a brand-new wild cat!

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: A new cat?! Like my neighbor's cat?

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: It LOOKS like a regular house cat! That's the funny part! People in Bolivia saw it for years and thought, oh, just a cute kitty!

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: Plot twist! It's NOT a kitty?

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: It's a whole new species! Called the Tilkayo tiger cat! It has leopard spots! And get this, it's the first new wild cat found in one hundred years!

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: One hundred years?! That's older than grandma!

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Ha ha! Way older! It's tiny, with round ears. So cute! Can you believe it?

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: Can I have one? Please please please?

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: It's wild, sweetie. But here's our word of the day: fossil. A fossil is what's left of an animal or plant from super long ago, turned into rock!

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: Like dinosaur bones?

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Exactly! Say it with us, friends! Fossil!

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: Fossil!

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: I love how you said that! Okay, story two! You know the Great Sphinx in Egypt? The giant lion with a human head?

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: The one with no nose?

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Ha! Yes! Well, scientists found a fossil INSIDE the rock the Sphinx is carved from!

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: Inside?! Was someone hiding it there?

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: It was waiting there for forty-five million years! It's a brand-new species of ancient crocodile with a super long, skinny snout! They named it after Horus, an Egyptian god!

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: A crocodile god?! Does it wear a crown?

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Ha ha ha! I love how you think! Maybe a tiny crown!

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: I knew it!

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Okay, last story, and it's my favorite! A Pikachu toy spent sixty-seven days in space!

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: WHAT?! Pikachu went to space?!

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Yes! It floated around the International Space Station for sixty-seven days! I know, it's amazing!

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: Did it catch any space Pokémon?

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Ha! Maybe! And now there's a Pokémon Space Trail at a museum in London, where kids learn about space with Pokémon!

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: I want to go! Can Pikachu be my teacher?

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Best teacher ever! Okay, it's game time!

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: Ooh, my favorite! Would you rather... cuddle the tiny Tilkayo tiger cat, or ride on the back of the giant fossil crocodile?

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Hmm, tough one... I'd cuddle the kitty! Those round ears! What about you, friends? Ask your mom and dad too!

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: I'd ride the crocodile! Giddy-up, Horus!

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Ha! I love it! Amazing choice!

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Thanks for hanging out with us! See you next time! Bye!

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: Bye! I'm going to find a fossil!

vocab.def: what's left of an animal or plant from long ago, turned into rock
a group of animals or plants that are all the same kind
vocab.ex_en: a new species of wild cat

vocab.def: the nose and mouth part of an animal
to stay in the air or on water without falling down

title: 小小英文新鲜事 - 1011 | 长角洛基海参、十月流星雨、爱泡澡的变形虫
ending_game: 小挑战:晴朗的夜晚和爸爸妈妈去户外看流星,抬头看天五分钟数数看到几颗,看到就许个愿!

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Hi friends! It is Sunday, October eleventh! I am Mia!

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: And I am Lina! Welcome to our little news show!

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Three fun stories today! First, down to the bottom of the sea!

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Scientists just found fifty seven brand new animals in the deep sea! Near Argentina, a giant underwater canyon called mar del PLAH-tuh drops three thousand five hundred meters down! A robot submarine named soo-BASS-chun explored it and found animals nobody had ever seen!

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: Fifty seven new animals? Did they find a mermaid?

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Ha ha! Not a mermaid, but something even funnier! A sea cucumber with little horns! Scientists named it Loki, like the tricky character, because its horns look mischievous!

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: Does it eat cucumbers? Can I keep one as a pet?

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Good question! They do not eat cucumbers! They are soft squishy crawlers of the sea floor. And this one lives in the dark, deep, cold sea — your bathtub is way too warm!

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: Aw! My rubber duck stays lonely then!

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Our second story is in the sky! October is meteor shower season! On a clear night, you might see shooting stars!

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: Shooting stars! I love them! Does someone throw them?

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Ha ha! Nobody throws them! Earth is flying through space dust left by a comet called HAL-eez. The dust hits our air, burns up, and makes a bright line of light! That is a shooting star!

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: So a shooting star is space dust going poof? Coolest poof ever!

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: It really is! Third story! In California, a park with volcanoes called LASS-en has pools of super hot water. Scientists found a tiny living thing there. They call it the fire amoeba!

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: Does it breathe fire? Can it roast marshmallows?

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: I know, it sounds crazy! It does not breathe fire, but it loves hot water! The water is one hundred forty five degrees, hotter than the hottest bath ever! Most living things would say ouch ouch ouch, but the fire amoeba says, ah, nice and warm!

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: One hundred forty five degrees? My toes say no no no!

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Ha ha! Smart toes! Now, friends, Word of the day! Today's word is meteor!

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: Meteor! Like the shooting star!

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Exactly! A meteor is a bright line of light in the sky when a tiny space rock burns up! Say it with us, friends! Mee-tee-or! Meteor!

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: Meteor! Do I get a prize?

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: You get a high five! Now our tiny challenge! On a clear night, go outside with your mom or dad and look up for five whole minutes! Count the shooting stars! See one? Make a wish!

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: Last time I saw one, I wished for ice cream! The next day we had ice cream! Coincidence? I think not!

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Ha ha! I love that! That is all for today, friends! See you next time!

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: Bye bye, friends! Keep looking up!

vocab.def: a bright line of light in the sky when a tiny space rock burns up
a deep, narrow valley — here, a giant one under the sea
a hard, pointy part growing on an animal's head
to burn completely until nothing is left
